process_area.title: Collections, Recourse Management, Reconciliation & Portfolio Analytics

value_stream.name: Trade Accounts Receivable Factoring, Invoice Discounting & Receivables Securitization

workflows.name: Factor/Funder Reconciliation, Fee/Interest Settlement & Monthly Account Statement

Automation Opportunity: - Factor statement auto-ingested and reconciled to BuildRight's records.
Controls: - CTL-19: funder-statement reconciliation; CTL-120 (fee/interest settlement accuracy); CTL-30 (close).
Cross-references: - links to VS-18 (treasury/fees), VS-17 (GL), VS-157 (financing income/expense)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unreconciled-difference risk**: unreconciled differences distort cash/fee/interest and the financials; mitigated by monthly reconciliation and discrepancy resolution.
- **Fee-leakage risk**: unchallenged incorrect factor fees/interest erode margin; mitigated by statement reconciliation and challenge of exceptions.
System Touchpoints: - Factoring reconciliation module; GL (VS-17); treasury/funding (VS-18); factor statement ingestion.

steps.activity: Receive the factor's monthly statement (advances, collections, fees, interest, reserve, recourse).
Reconcile the statement to BuildRight's records (submissions W5401, drawdowns W5402, collections W5404).
Settle fees/interest and reserve per the facility terms; post to GL (VS-17/VS-157).
Investigate and resolve discrepancies with the factor (timing, fees, reserve).
Report reconciliation status and any open items to the treasury committee (W5416).

workflows.name: Receivables Aging, Sub-Limits, Concentration & Pool Health Monitoring

Controls: - CTL-799 (ensure controlled execution — Collections, Recourse Management, Reconciliation & Portfolio Analytics (PA-189.3).)
- operational: aging accuracy; CTL-35 (concentration-limit adherence); CTL-23 (fraud detection).
Pain Points / Risks: - **Covenant-breach risk**: breaching concentration/dilution/delinquency covenants triggers facility recourse/termination; mitigated by monitoring and early corrective action.
- **Concentration risk**: over-exposure to a customer/segment magnifies default/recourse impact; mitigated by sub-limits and concentration monitoring.
System Touchpoints: - Credit-risk/aging analytics (VS-68); concentration/covenant dashboard; factoring pool health.

steps.activity: Monitor factored-receivables aging and delinquency by customer/segment.
Check concentration vs. sub-limits (W5395) and facility thresholds; flag breaches.
Monitor pool health (collections rate, dilution, recourse rate) vs. facility covenants/triggers.
Take corrective action on breaches (curtail submission, restructure, cure).
Report portfolio health to the credit/treasury committee and funder (W5408/W5416).

fields.Participants: Credit Manager, Compliance Specialist, Customer, Trade Account Manager (VS-107), Factor
fields.Trigger: Customer query/dispute on a notified factored invoice; audit/inspection

workflows.name: Customer Notification Compliance, Audit-Trail & Dispute/Query Handling

Automation Opportunity: - Query workflow with auto-pulled assignment audit-trail.
Controls: - CTL-799 (ensure controlled execution — Collections, Recourse Management, Reconciliation & Portfolio Analytics (PA-189.3).)
- operational: assignment accuracy; CTL-27 (customer data); CTL-41 (audit-trail completeness).
Cross-references: - links to VS-16 (AR/disputes), VS-107 (accounts), VS-88 (records), VS-100 (legal/assignment)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Notification-error risk**: a remit/assignment error causes customer confusion, mis-directed payment, and dispute volume; mitigated by audit-trail verification and process fix.
- **Audit-trail-gap risk**: missing assignment/notification evidence undermines enforceability and audit; mitigated by maintained records (VS-88).
System Touchpoints: - AR/customer records (VS-16/VS-29); assignment audit-trail (VS-88); dispute/query module.

steps.activity: Receive customer query/dispute on a notified factored invoice (remit, amount, assignment).
Verify the assignment/notification audit-trail (W5396/W5400) and remit accuracy (W5403).
Resolve the query with the customer and factor; correct any remit/notification error.
Maintain the assignment/notification audit-trail for inspection (VS-88/VS-21).
Escalate systemic notification issues (W5396) for process fix.

fields.Participants: Credit Manager, Finance Controller, External Auditor, CFO
fields.Trigger: Monthly close; recourse/buyback activity (W5407); credit deterioration

workflows.name: Recourse Exposure, Bad-Debt Buyback Reserve & ECL Provisioning (PFRS 9)

Automation Opportunity: - ECL auto-computed from recourse/aging/risk data with documented methodology.
Controls: - CTL-31: adequate provisions; CTL-30 (close); CTL-21 (accuracy); CTL-29 (consolidated reporting).
Cross-references: - links to VS-157 (revenue/loss), VS-17 (GL), VS-68 (credit), VS-21 (audit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-provisioning risk**: an inadequate ECL/reserve on recourse exposure distorts the audited PFRS financials; mitigated by documented methodology and audit confirmation.
- **Recourse-loss risk**: recourse losses above reserve erode program economics; mitigated by reserve sizing and portfolio risk management (W5410).

steps.activity: Compute recourse exposure and expected credit loss (ECL) on recourse/bought-back receivables under PFRS 9.
Size the bad-debt/buyback reserve from recourse history and portfolio risk (W5399).
Post the ECL provision and reserve to GL (VS-17); document methodology.
Reconcile provisions to credit-risk and recourse activity (W5407).
Confirm methodology with the external auditor annually (VS-21).

fields.Participants: TPRM Analyst, CFO, TPRM (VS-161), Credit Manager, Finance

workflows.name: Factor Performance, Dispute Rate & Service-Level Monitoring

Controls: - CTL-799 (ensure controlled execution — Collections, Recourse Management, Reconciliation & Portfolio Analytics (PA-189.3).)
Cross-references: - links to VS-161 (TPRM), VS-18 (treasury), VS-67 (vendor scorecard pattern)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Funder-deterioration risk**: a factor's operational/financial deterioration disrupts funding; mitigated by TPRM monitoring and alternative-funder readiness.
- **Service-cost risk**: poor factor service (slow funding, disputes) raises effective cost; mitigated by performance monitoring and challenge.
System Touchpoints: - Vendor/factor performance analytics; TPRM inventory (VS-161); reconciliation data (W5409).

steps.activity: Track factor performance: funding speed, dispute/rejection rate, fee accuracy, and service responsiveness.
TPRM-monitor the factor/funder (financial standing, operational issues) — VS-161.
Address service-level breaches and recurring disputes with the factor.
Evaluate factor alternatives and rebalance funding mix if performance is poor (W5414).
Report factor performance to the treasury committee.

fields.Participants: CFO, Treasury, CEO, Treasury, Credit Manager, CFO, BI (VS-28)

workflows.name: Receivables-Sale P&L, Cost-of-Funds vs. Discount Analytics & Funding-Mix Optimization

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-refreshing program P&L and cost-of-funds dashboard.
Controls: - CTL-799 (ensure controlled execution — Collections, Recourse Management, Reconciliation & Portfolio Analytics (PA-189.3).)
- operational: profitability-data accuracy; CTL-35 (vs. business case); CTL-19 (treasury reconciliation).
Cross-references: - links to VS-18 (treasury), VS-17 (P&L), VS-170 (ABL/mix), VS-105 (SCF), VS-28 (BI), VS-36/VS-173 (board)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin-erosion risk**: rising recourse losses or fees compress program margin below target; mitigated by P&L monitoring and funding-mix optimization.
- **Sub-optimal-mix risk**: using high-cost factoring when lower-cost discounting/ABL would suffice; mitigated by cost-of-funds analytics.
System Touchpoints: - Treasury/funding analytics (VS-18); profitability dashboard (VS-28/VS-17); board reporting (VS-36/VS-173).

steps.activity: Compute program P&L: financing income net of discount/fees, recourse losses, and operating cost.
Analyze cost-of-funds vs. discount across instruments (factoring vs. discounting vs. ABL — VS-170).
Optimize the funding mix (shift to lower-cost instruments where risk permits).
Compare to the business case (W5393) and risk-appetite targets; flag erosion.
Report program profitability to the treasury/finance committee and board (VS-36/VS-173).

fields.Participants: CFO, Internal Audit, Compliance Specialist, VP Legal & Compliance, CEO, Internal Audit (VS-21), Compliance, External Auditor, CFO
fields.Trigger: Annual audit plan; BSP/SEC/tax examination; internal-audit cycle

workflows.name: Internal Controls, Audit & Regulatory Examination Support

Automation Opportunity: - Audit-evidence package auto-assembled from the factoring platform and GL.
Controls: - CTL-799 (ensure controlled execution — Collections, Recourse Management, Reconciliation & Portfolio Analytics (PA-189.3).)
- operational: statutory compliance; regulatory; internal-audit independence (VS-21); accuracy; consolidated reporting; .
Cross-references: - links to VS-21 (audit), VS-22 (compliance), VS-157 (PFRS 9), VS-88 (records), VS-36/VS-173 (board), VS-100 (legal)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Examination-finding risk**: an examination that finds weak eligibility/reconciliation/derecognition controls triggers regulatory/audit action; mitigated by annual internal audit and control testing.
- **Re-characterization risk**: audit/regulatory re-characterization of a "sale" as a borrowing changes the financials and leverage; mitigated by substance monitoring (W5397) and true-sale opinion.
System Touchpoints: - Audit-findings register (VS-21); records retention (VS-88); PFRS-9 accounting evidence (W5397).
Time Estimate: - ~3–4 weeks per annual audit; per examination.

steps.activity: Maintain the controls framework: eligibility, submission, drawdown, reconciliation, recourse, provisioning.
Support internal audit testing of factoring controls (separation, reconciliation, derecognition).
On BSP/SEC/tax examination: provide facility, submission, reconciliation, and PFRS-9 derecognition evidence.
Document and remediate findings; track to closure (VS-21/VS-22).
Escalate material findings/regulatory action to the board (VS-36/VS-173).

fields.Participants: Treasury Lead, CFO, Finance Business Partner, CEO, Credit Manager, BI (VS-28)

workflows.name: Portfolio Cash-Conversion-Cycle, DSO Impact & Treasury Integration Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-refreshing CCC/DSO dashboard integrated into the group cash-flow forecast.
Controls: - CTL-799 (ensure controlled execution — Collections, Recourse Management, Reconciliation & Portfolio Analytics (PA-189.3).)
- operational: working-capital-data accuracy; CTL-35 (vs. plan); CTL-19 (treasury reconciliation).
Cross-references: - links to VS-18 (treasury/cash), VS-105 (SCF/working capital), VS-170 (ABL), VS-28 (BI), VS-36/VS-173 (board)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over/under-financing risk**: too much factoring (high cost) or too little (cash strain) mis-optimizes working capital; mitigated by CCC/DSO analytics and tuning.
- **Forecast-integration risk**: the program not integrated into the group cash forecast causes funding surprises; mitigated by treasury integration.
System Touchpoints: - Treasury/cash-flow forecast (VS-18); working-capital analytics (VS-105/VS-170); BI (VS-28); board reporting (VS-36/VS-173).

steps.activity: Compute the program's cash-conversion-cycle and DSO impact (cash released vs. un-financed baseline).
Integrate the factoring program into the group cash-flow forecast and funding plan (VS-18).
Analyze the working-capital benefit vs. program cost (W5414) and risk transfer.
Identify opportunities to expand/contract the program based on cash need and cost (W5393).
Report working-capital impact to the treasury committee and board (VS-36/VS-173).
